why: What a cloud-submitted wave actually covers has two independent tellers, and
an operator hears whichever one they happen to be standing in front of:
cmd/tk/cmd/cloud.go (the ignite verb, before the push) and
cloud/factory/src/run-workflow.ts (the run's own status, its dispatch log and
the reason its closeout orchestrator is given). Tick wiy exists because the
claim was made in neither: context.cloud_wave is resolved ONCE from
params.tick_ids and the closeout pass never re-derives or re-dispatches a
second cloud wave, so an epic needing more than one wave gets per-tick
containers for the first wave only — and 'Phase 2: cloud substrate fan-out'
reads like a promise that every wave fans out. Deriving waves 2+ in the
Worker would mean porting readiness into TypeScript, which the design doc
decided against (see 'Where does wave.Compute run for the dispatcher?'), so
the honest half is what ships: say it plainly, everywhere, in one sentence
both tellers are pinned to. Two surfaces phrasing the same limit two ways is
how the limit stops being legible.
note: fan-out is first-wave-only: this run dispatches exactly one wave of per-tick containers, and every tick it does not name — including ticks this wave unblocks — is implemented as a harness subagent inside the closeout orchestrator's single sandbox rather than as its own container
